title: The Covering We Do Not See

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle — eleven altogether. All eleven curtains are to be the same size — thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. Join five of the curtains together into one set and the other six into another set. Fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent." - Exodus 26:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Over the beautiful embroidered curtains came a second layer — plain curtains of goat hair. No blue and purple yarn here, no woven cherubim. Just sturdy, practical goat hair, made to sit over the top where its purpose was protection rather than display. It covered the beauty and took the weather.

There is something quietly moving about this layer. It was the least impressive material mentioned, yet it did essential work. The gorgeous inner curtains stayed beautiful precisely because something plainer stood between them and the harsh desert sky. Not every necessary thing is a beautiful thing.

Many of God's people serve like goat-hair curtains. They are not the visible, admired parts of church life. They set up chairs, pray quietly, clean up afterwards, support others behind the scenes. Nobody photographs the goat hair. But God specified it, measured it, and gave it a place in His dwelling. Scripture reminds us that the parts of the body which seem less honourable are treated with special honour by God (1 Cor 12:23-24). If your service feels unseen, take heart — the covering layer matters, and God has not overlooked it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I resent serving in ways no one notices?
Who around me does unseen work that I could recognise and thank?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You give value to what the world overlooks. Help me serve faithfully even when unseen, trusting that You notice and that my part matters in Your house. Amen.
